relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: In voltage clamp recordings from human DRG neurons, suzetrigine was shown to block human NaV1.8 channels with an IC50 of 0.68 nM [2].

relationships.subject: suzetrigine
relationships.evidence_quote: In current clamp recordings, the selective NaV1.8 blocker suzetrigine reduced repetitive action potential firing in a dose-dependent manner during depolarization, but did not completely eliminate it.

relationships.subject: metformin
relationships.evidence_quote: earlier work demonstrated that metformin downregulates NaV1.7 expression via the ubiquitin ligase NEDD4-2 [26]

relationships.subject: TRPV1
relationships.evidence_quote: Additional evidence comes from clinical studies showing that intra-articular administration of TRPV1 agonists provides significant pain relief in OA patients [28].

key_findings: Broad NaV subtype redundancy in human DRG neurons explains the limited efficacy of selective NaV1.8 blockade by suzetrigine.
Human genetics and multi-omics, plus site-of-action and PK/PD validation, are proposed as a framework for selecting analgesic targets.
